clue.text: Underwear in state: groom is wearing it!

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it

indicators.note: the state sits in the middle of the next two letters
the letters of 'is' have the state on them, as a body has clothes on

parts.note: taken as written
a state is a nation

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone getting married in their state finery, with the groom in an all-in-one undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: Combinations are an old-fashioned one-piece undergarment covering body and legs, much like a union suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinations are a single garment joining vest and long drawers, worn as underclothing.

clue.text: Heavyweights in defeat saved by endless cash

indicators.note: the defeat is held inside the cash, as savings are kept
the last letter is removed

parts.note: coin is money in metal form
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Big hitters who would have lost if not rescued by money.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are giant statues or figures, so the word stands for anything of huge size or importance.

clue.text: Economist and poet taking cannibal's food?

parts.note: John Milton wrote Paradise Lost
a fried man would be a dish for a cannibal

explanation.surface: Asks whether an economist and a poet are on a cannibal's menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname splits into FRIED MAN, a meal for a cannibal.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman was the American Nobel laureate who championed monetarism.

clue.text: Dream what croupier might say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a perfect thing one hopes for
second meaning: read as two words, '...', as a card dealer at a casino might announce

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into two words, the question mark admitting the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect standard one aspires to, and a croupier deals the cards.

clue.text: Old general I pass invading Indian city

indicators.note: the two pieces force their way into the city's name

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
taken as written
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A historical general moving through a mountain pass to storm an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal; a col is a pass between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was the Roman general who governed Britain and campaigned in Scotland.

clue.text: Suspect provided that case of felony

parts.note: 'if' means on condition that

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word form its casing

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A legal note on when someone might be a suspect in a felony case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' is an adjective here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious, just as something suspect is questionable.

clue.text: Square packing crate designed for fruit

indicators.note: the square holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new design

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A square crate built for transporting fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: One's neither civil nor polite, but rude or foul!

definitions.meaning: civil and polite have five and six letters, so neither is the kind of word meant
rude and foul both have four letters, and a swear word is rude and foul

explanation.surface: Describes a swear word: never courteous, always coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters: civil and polite are too long, rude and foul are exactly the length the answer's first part names.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-letter word is a swear word, many common obscenities having four letters.

clue.text: Magnate ending in family business, significant amount's banked

indicators.note: the other pieces are deposited inside the large amount

parts.note: a ton is informal for a large amount

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: its last letter only

explanation.surface: A business tycoon with a family firm and a large sum in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful businessman, also called a magnate.

clue.text: French city, former Olympic hosts cancelling field event?

indicators.note: the field event is struck out of the hosts' name, leaving what remains

parts.note: Lillehammer in Norway hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics
the hammer throw is an athletics field event

explanation.surface: A French city replacing the former Olympic hosts and dropping one of the athletics events.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'field event' is a part of the Norwegian town's name rather than a sport being scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Worshipper's place in which food eaten, primarily?

definitions.text: Worshipper's place in which food eaten, primarily?

indicators.note: the opening letters go inside the clergy house

parts.note: a rectory is the house of a rector, a parish clergyman

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of these two words is used

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Asks whether a church building is chiefly a place for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: a refectory is the dining hall of a monastery, a worshipper's place where food is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a communal dining room, originally in a monastery or college.

clue.text: Each sole mended — string nearby?

indicators.note: a mended shoe has its parts reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cobbler repairs every sole and wonders whether there is some string to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cheeky: a lace is a string found near the sole of a shoe, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoelace is a cord threaded through a shoe's eyelets, sitting close to the sole being mended.

clue.text: Interruption of testing by India leader of opposition dreads, say?

definitions.note: singular: dreadlocks are one example of a hairstyle

indicators.note: the letter for India breaks into the middle of the word for testing

parts.note: a testing task is a hard one

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'opposition' is taken

parts.note: its first letter only

explanation.surface: A political scene: the opposition leader dreads India interrupting a test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreads' reads as a verb but is the noun for dreadlocks; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a particular style in which hair is worn, so they are one kind of hairstyle.

clue.text: People who don't believe lies find another way

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a different way from how they stand

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sceptics who catch out falsehoods by looking at them differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are unbelievers, those without the religious faith of the speaker.

clue.text: Harsh critic in debate "discontented" with vehicle

indicators.note: the word's contents are emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters, the middle emptied out
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An unhappy fierce critic in a debate about a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'discontented' is to be read literally as 'without its contents'.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor is someone who disparages or belittles another's worth.

clue.text: For example, Homer's Greek character gone travelling

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the letters set off and move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reference to a character from Homer's Greek epics who has gone off on a journey, like Odysseus.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer is not the poet: a homer is a homing pigeon. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, trained to fly back to its loft over long distances.

clue.text: Create flier that's OK

parts.note: to forge is to make or shape
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: Someone making a leaflet and asking if it is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a leaflet but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'forget it' dismisses an apology or thanks, meaning no harm done.

clue.text: Foxy observed mousy collecting newspapers

indicators.note: the shy word gathers the two papers into its middle

parts.note: a mousy person is timid and shy
the i and the FT (Financial Times) are two British daily papers, put side by side

explanation.surface: Someone sly is seen with a timid person gathering up the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily paper and the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy means cunning or sly, like a fox, and a shifty person looks deceitful.

clue.text: Toil over an advertising expression

indicators.note: in a down clue the toil sits above the next piece

parts.note: to slog is to work hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: Working hard on an advertising catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a memorable phrase used in advertising or campaigning.

clue.text: Family dispute — help!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to do with the home or household
second meaning: a quarrel, especially between partners at home

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one headline it is a family row with a cry for help; the three words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for household life, informal British for a row at home, and a noun for a servant.

clue.text: Money to invest, sterling

definitions.meaning: first meaning: funds available for investment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterling' tempts as British currency, but here it is the old-fashioned praise word for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the noun for invested funds and a dated British adjective for splendid.

clue.text: Reportedly, foreign water perhaps does well!

indicators.note: the words are heard as spoken, not as spelt, and this covers both sounds

parts.note: eau is French for water
does (female deer) are an example of deer

explanation.surface: Commentary that some foreign water is good for you, perhaps a spa advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is not the verb but the plural of doe; 'well' is an exclamation, not health.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections expressing surprise or mild disappointment.

clue.text: A good appeal: support promotion of communism

parts.note: taken as written
'it' is old slang for sex appeal
a prop holds something up

explanation.surface: Political slogans: a fine appeal backing communist propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, originally from the Soviet department of agitation and propaganda.

clue.text: Sign name to take claims up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top
the words lay claim to the letters, holding them within

parts.note: the letters run across the end of 'name', all of 'to' and the start of 'take'

explanation.surface: Signing one's name to take on some claims.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards through the end of 'name', 'to' and the start of 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol, revered as the sign of a clan.

clue.text: Shop fronts on dreary estate look inadequate

indicators.note: the front letter of each word is taken

parts.note: its first letter
its first letter
its first letter
its first letter

explanation.surface: Shopfronts on a run-down estate look poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, sells cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Flat passage in requiem, initially erased

indicators.note: the passage goes inside what is left
the first letter of the lament is rubbed out

parts.note: a requiem is a lament for the dead
a part is a passage of music or text

explanation.surface: A dull passage of a requiem, with its opening wiped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a musical adjective but is the noun for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartment is the usual American word for a flat, a set of rooms on one floor.

clue.text: Purple's second and blue's third in red fish

indicators.note: the shared letter goes inside the left-winger

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-winger or red
its second letter is the same as the third letter of 'blue', so the shared letter is taken once

explanation.surface: Colour notes on a fish that is purple, blue and red.
explanation.walkthrough: Purple's second letter and blue's third are the same letter, used once. A Trot is a Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are freshwater fish of the salmon family, prized by anglers.

clue.text: Sit with old master sprawling — might one?

definitions.text: Sit with old master sprawling — might one?

indicators.note: spread out untidily, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wonders whether someone would pose lounging beside a great painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an artist's model might well sit sprawled with an old master.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model poses for a painter, often sitting or reclining as instructed.
